questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$ has lowest boiling point ?
questions.solution:
The boiling point of isomeric alcohols decreases with an increase in branching.

As branching increases, the molecule becomes more spherical in shape, which decreases the effective surface area.

A smaller surface area results in weaker van der Waals forces of attraction between the molecules, thereby lowering the boiling point.

Among the given isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$, tert-butyl alcohol is the most branched.

Therefore, tert-butyl alcohol has the lowest boiling point.

Answer: tert Butyl alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Select the correct decreasing order of acid strength for the following compounds.
a) Ethanol   b) 2-Methyl propan-2-ol   c) Phenol   d) p - Nitrophenol
questions.solution:
Acid strength is directly proportional to the stability of the conjugate base formed after the removal of an $H^+$ ion.

The conjugate bases are:
a) Ethoxide ion ($CH_3CH_2O^-$)
b) tert-Butoxide ion ($(CH_3)_3CO^-$)
c) Phenoxide ion ($C_6H_5O^-$)
d) p-Nitrophenoxide ion ($p-NO_2-C_6H_4O^-$)

Phenoxide ions are resonance stabilized, making phenols more acidic than aliphatic alcohols. Thus, (c) and (d) are more acidic than (a) and (b).

In p-nitrophenol (d), the $-NO_2$ group exerts strong $-I$ and $-R$ effects, which further stabilizes the phenoxide ion. Hence, p-nitrophenol is more acidic than phenol (c).

Among the alcohols, the $+I$ effect of the alkyl groups destabilizes the alkoxide ion. The tert-butyl group in 2-methylpropan-2-ol (b) exerts a stronger $+I$ effect than the ethyl group in ethanol (a). Therefore, ethanol is more acidic than 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

The correct decreasing order of acid strength is d > c > a > b.

Answer: d > c > a > b

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the 'product' in the following reaction.
Pent - 3 - enenitrile $\xrightarrow[\large{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}]{\large{\text{Al H (i-Bu)}_2}}$ Product
questions.solution:
The given reactant is pent-3-enenitrile, which has the structure $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CN}$.

Diisobutylaluminium hydride (DIBAL-H), represented as $\text{AlH(i-Bu)}_2$, is a selective reducing agent. It reduces nitriles to imines at low temperatures, which upon subsequent acidic hydrolysis ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$) yield aldehydes.

DIBAL-H does not reduce isolated carbon-carbon double bonds.

The reaction proceeds as follows:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{N} \xrightarrow{\text{AlH(i-Bu)}_2} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{N}-\text{Al(i-Bu)}_2$

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{N}-\text{Al(i-Bu)}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$

The final product is pent-3-enal.

Answer: Pent - 3 - enal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amines when heated with ethanolic KOH and chloroform does NOT produce foul smell ?
questions.solution:
The reaction of an amine with chloroform and ethanolic KOH to produce a foul-smelling compound is known as the carbylamine test or isocyanide test.

This test is given only by primary aliphatic and primary aromatic amines. Secondary and tertiary amines do not respond to this test.

Benzenamine is a primary aromatic amine.

Propan-2-amine is a primary aliphatic amine.

Phenylmethanamine is a primary aliphatic amine.

N,N-Dimethyl aniline is a tertiary amine, so it does not give the carbylamine test and will not produce a foul smell.

Answer: N , N - Dimethyl aniline

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify 'B' in the following reaction
Ethyl cyanide $\xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}_2\text{O}}} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}_2\text{O / dil HCl}}} \text{B} + \text{NH}_3$
questions.solution:
Ethyl cyanide is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$.

Partial hydrolysis of ethyl cyanide yields propanamide (A).

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$

Complete hydrolysis of propanamide in the presence of dilute $\text{HCl}$ yields propanoic acid (B) and ammonia.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O} / \text{dil HCl}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_3$

Therefore, B is propanoic acid.

Answer: Propanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of moles of hydrogen atoms needed to obtain one mole ethanamine from acetamide using $\text{LiAl H}_4$ /ether as reducing agent.
questions.solution:
The chemical reaction for the reduction of acetamide to ethanamine using $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is:

$\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2 + 4[\text{H}] \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4/\text{ether}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

In this process, the carbonyl oxygen is removed as a water molecule, which consumes two hydrogen atoms. The carbonyl carbon is reduced to a methylene group ($\text{CH}_2$), which consumes another two hydrogen atoms.

Thus, a total of $4$ moles of hydrogen atoms are required to reduce one mole of acetamide to one mole of ethanamine.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a protein present in nails
questions.solution:
Keratin is a tough, fibrous structural protein that forms the main structural constituent of hair, feathers, hooves, claws, horns, and nails.

Legumelin is a protein found in leguminous plants.

Myosin is a motor protein found in muscles that is responsible for muscle contraction.

Insulin is a peptide hormone produced by the pancreas that regulates blood sugar levels.

Answer: Keratin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify glycosidic linkage in lactose.
questions.solution:
Lactose is a disaccharide composed of $\beta$-D-galactose and $\beta$-D-glucose.

The glycosidic linkage is formed between C1 of $\beta$-D-galactose and C4 of $\beta$-D-glucose.

Therefore, the glycosidic linkage in lactose is $\beta-1,4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when isopropyl magnesium chloride in dry ether reacts with dry ice forming a complex, hydrolysed further.
questions.solution:
Isopropyl magnesium chloride is $(CH_3)_2CHMgCl$.

Dry ice is solid $CO_2$.

When a Grignard reagent reacts with dry ice, it undergoes nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl group of $CO_2$ to form a magnesium carboxylate complex.

$(CH_3)_2CHMgCl + O=C=O \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CH-COOMgCl$

Upon acid hydrolysis, the complex yields a carboxylic acid.

$(CH_3)_2CH-COOMgCl + H_2O \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CH-COOH + Mg(OH)Cl$

The product $(CH_3)_2CH-COOH$ is 2-methylpropanoic acid.

Answer: 2 - Methylpropanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ethers is gaseous at room temperature ?
questions.solution:
Dimethyl ether and ethyl methyl ether (methoxyethane) are gases at room temperature.

Other lower homologues of ethers, such as diethyl ether (ethoxyethane), 1-methoxypropane, and 1-ethoxypropane, are colourless, highly volatile liquids at room temperature.

Therefore, methoxyethane is gaseous at room temperature.

Answer: Methoxyethane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following gases is least soluble in water at same temperature and pressure ?
questions.solution:
Solubility of a gas in water depends on its ability to interact with water molecules. Water is a polar solvent.

$\text{NH}_3$ is highly soluble in water due to its ability to form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water.

$\text{HCl}$ is a polar molecule that ionizes completely in water, making it highly soluble.

$\text{CO}_2$ is moderately soluble because it reacts with water to form carbonic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$).

$\text{N}_2$ is a non-polar diatomic gas that neither reacts with water nor forms hydrogen bonds. Therefore, it has the weakest interaction with water molecules and is the least soluble among the given gases.

Answer: $\text{N}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement from the following.
options: In $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{NF}_3$ the orbital dipole due to lone pair is in the same direction as that of resultant dipole moment of other three bonds
Dipole moment of $\text{NH}_3$ is greater than $\text{NF}_3$
questions.solution:
Both $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{NF}_3$ have a central nitrogen atom with $sp^3$ hybridization and one lone pair, giving them a trigonal pyramidal shape. Both are polar molecules.

In $\text{NH}_3$, nitrogen is more electronegative than hydrogen. The bond dipole moments of the three N-H bonds are directed towards the nitrogen atom. Their resultant dipole moment is in the same direction as the orbital dipole due to the lone pair, leading to a higher net dipole moment.

In $\text{NF}_3$, fluorine is more electronegative than nitrogen. The bond dipole moments of the three N-F bonds are directed towards the fluorine atoms. Their resultant dipole moment is in the opposite direction to the orbital dipole due to the lone pair. This partial cancellation results in a lower net dipole moment for $\text{NF}_3$ compared to $\text{NH}_3$.

Therefore, the statement that the orbital dipole due to the lone pair is in the same direction as the resultant dipole moment of the three bonds in both molecules is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a reaction $\text{A} \longrightarrow$ product, $k = 2 \times 10^{-2}\ \text{s}^{-1}$. If the initial concentration of A is $1.0\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$ find the value of $\log \dfrac{1}{[A]_t}$ after 100 second ?
questions.solution:
The unit of rate constant $k$ is $\text{s}^{-1}$, indicating that the reaction is of first order.

For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate equation is:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t}$

Substituting the given values $k = 2 \times 10^{-2}\ \text{s}^{-1}$, $t = 100\ \text{s}$, and $[A]_0 = 1.0\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$:

$2 \times 10^{-2} = \dfrac{2.303}{100} \log \dfrac{1.0}{[A]_t}$

$2 \times 10^{-2} \times 100 = 2.303 \log \dfrac{1}{[A]_t}$

$2 = 2.303 \log \dfrac{1}{[A]_t}$

$\log \dfrac{1}{[A]_t} = \dfrac{2}{2.303} = 0.868$

Answer: $0.868$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the time required for 75 % completion of a first order reaction if rate constant is $23.03\ \text{minute}^{-1}$ ?
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the time required for a given completion is given by:

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a-x} \right)$

Given $k = 23.03 \text{ min}^{-1}$ and for $75\%$ completion, $x = 0.75a$.

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{23.03} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a - 0.75a} \right)$

$t = 0.1 \log \left( \dfrac{1}{0.25} \right)$

$t = 0.1 \log 4$

$t = 0.1 \times 0.602 = 0.0602 \text{ min}$

Converting the time into seconds:

$t = 0.0602 \times 60 \text{ s} = 3.612 \text{ s} \approx 3.6 \text{ s}$

Answer: $3.6$ s

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of fractional order reaction ?
questions.solution:
The decomposition of acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) is a well-known example of a fractional order reaction.

The experimentally determined rate law for this reaction is given by:

$\text{Rate} = k[\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}]^{1.5}$

Thus, the overall order of the reaction is $1.5$, which is a fractional value.

For the other given reactions:
Decomposition of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is a first-order reaction.
Formation of $\text{HI}$ from $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{I}_2$ is a second-order reaction.
Reaction between $\text{NO}$ and $\text{H}_2$ is a third-order reaction.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_4\text{(g)} + \text{CO}\text{(g)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following plants is useful to extract analgesic compound from it ?
questions.solution:
Wintergreen oil contains methyl salicylate, which is widely used as an analgesic compound in various pain-relieving ointments and balms.

Turmeric contains curcumin, which is primarily known for its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties.

Cinnamon contains cinnamaldehyde, used mainly as a flavoring agent and has antimicrobial properties.

Citrus fruits are rich in citric acid and vitamin C.

Therefore, wintergreen is the plant useful for extracting an analgesic compound.

Answer: Wintergreen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a correct increasing order of ligand field strength ?
questions.solution:
According to the spectrochemical series, the ligands are arranged in the increasing order of their crystal field splitting energy (CFSE) or ligand field strength as follows:

$I^{-} \lt Br^{-} \lt SCN^{-} \lt Cl^{-} \lt S^{2-} \lt F^{-} \lt OH^{-} \lt C_2O_4^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt NCS^{-} \lt EDTA^{4-} \lt NH_3 \lt en \lt CN^{-} \lt CO$

From the given options, the correct increasing order of ligand field strength is:

$C_2O_4^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt EDTA \lt en$

Answer: $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \lt \text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{EDTA} \lt \text{en}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is EAN for metal ion in $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ ?
questions.solution:
The atomic number of iron (Fe) is $26$.

Let the oxidation state of Fe in $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ be $x$.

$x + 6(-1) = -3$

$x = +3$

The formula for Effective Atomic Number (EAN) is:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{Oxidation state} + 2 \times (\text{Coordination number})$

$\text{EAN} = 26 - 3 + 2 \times 6$

$\text{EAN} = 23 + 12 = 35$

Answer: $35$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which lanthanoid from following exhibits $f^{14}$ configuration in +3 state?
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of Lutetium (Lu), which has an atomic number of $71$, is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{14} 5d^{1} 6s^{2}$.

In the $+3$ oxidation state, Lu loses two electrons from the $6s$ orbital and one electron from the $5d$ orbital.

Therefore, the electronic configuration of $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{14}$.

For the other given elements in their $+3$ state:
$\text{Tm}^{3+}$ ($Z=69$) has the configuration $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{12}$.
$\text{Ce}^{3+}$ ($Z=58$) has the configuration $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{1}$.
$\text{Dy}^{3+}$ ($Z=66$) has the configuration $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{9}$.

Answer: Lu

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following pair of elements in their respective oxidation states have same number of unpaired electrons ?
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of $\text{Fe}$ ($Z=26$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6 4s^2$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$. It has $4$ unpaired electrons.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}$ ($Z=25$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5$. It has $5$ unpaired electrons.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}$ ($Z=27$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7 4s^2$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7$. It has $3$ unpaired electrons.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Ni}$ ($Z=28$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^2$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$. It has $2$ unpaired electrons.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Cr}$ ($Z=24$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^1$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4$. It has $4$ unpaired electrons.

Thus, $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ both have $4$ unpaired electrons.

Answer: $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cr}^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If standard reduction potential of four electrodes A, B, C, D are $+2.5\,\text{V}, +3.0\,\text{V}, -2.0\,\text{V}$ and $-1.5\,\text{V}$ respectively. When is the standard emf of cell maximum?
questions.solution:
The standard emf of a cell is given by $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{\circ}_{\text{anode}}$.

To obtain the maximum standard emf, the cathode must have the highest standard reduction potential and the anode must have the lowest standard reduction potential.

Given standard reduction potentials are:
$E^{\circ}_{\text{A}} = +2.5\text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{B}} = +3.0\text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{C}} = -2.0\text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{D}} = -1.5\text{ V}$

The highest reduction potential is for electrode B ($+3.0\text{ V}$), so B should act as the cathode.

The lowest reduction potential is for electrode C ($-2.0\text{ V}$), so C should act as the anode.

Maximum $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = 3.0 - (-2.0) = 5.0\text{ V}$.

Thus, 'C' is the anode and 'B' is the cathode.

Answer: 'C' is anode and 'B' is cathode

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
If standard reduction potential of Zn, Ni and Fe are $-0.76\,\text{V}$, $-0.23\,\text{V}$ and $-0.44\,\text{V}$ respectively. For the reaction (Stated below) to be spontaneous find out electrodes X and Y considering above electrode potentials
$\text{X}_{(s)} + \text{Y}^{+2}_{(aq)} \longrightarrow \text{X}^{+2}_{(aq)} + \text{Y}_{(s)}$
questions.solution:
For the given reaction $\text{X}_{(s)} + \text{Y}^{+2}_{(aq)} \longrightarrow \text{X}^{+2}_{(aq)} + \text{Y}_{(s)}$, X undergoes oxidation and acts as the anode, while Y undergoes reduction and acts as the cathode.

For the reaction to be spontaneous, the standard cell potential $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}$ must be positive.

$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{\circ}_{\text{anode}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{Y}} - E^{\circ}_{\text{X}} \gt 0$

This implies $E^{\circ}_{\text{Y}} \gt E^{\circ}_{\text{X}}$.

Given standard reduction potentials:
$E^{\circ}_{\text{Zn}} = -0.76\,\text{V}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{Ni}} = -0.23\,\text{V}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{Fe}} = -0.44\,\text{V}$

Checking the given options:
If X = Ni, Y = Fe: $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = -0.44 - (-0.23) = -0.21\,\text{V}$ (Non-spontaneous)
If X = Ni, Y = Zn: $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = -0.76 - (-0.23) = -0.53\,\text{V}$ (Non-spontaneous)
If X = Fe, Y = Zn: $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = -0.76 - (-0.44) = -0.32\,\text{V}$ (Non-spontaneous)
If X = Zn, Y = Ni: $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = -0.23 - (-0.76) = +0.53\,\text{V}$ (Spontaneous)

Thus, the reaction is spontaneous when X = Zn and Y = Ni.

Answer: X = Zn , Y = Ni

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A galvanic cell consist copper electrode and standard hydrogen electrode. If $E^\circ\left(\text{Cu}^{+2}_{(aq)} | \text{Cu}_{(s)}\right) = +0.34\,\text{V}$, then identify a reaction taking place at positive electrode during working of cell.
questions.solution:
Given $E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{+2}/\text{Cu}) = +0.34\,\text{V}$ and $E^\circ(\text{H}^+/\text{H}_2) = 0.00\,\text{V}$.

Since the standard reduction potential of the copper electrode is greater than that of the standard hydrogen electrode, copper acts as the cathode and the hydrogen electrode acts as the anode.

In a galvanic cell, the cathode is the positive electrode where reduction takes place.

The reduction reaction at the positive electrode (copper cathode) is:

$\text{Cu}^{+2}_{(aq)} + 2e^- \longrightarrow \text{Cu}_{(s)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds does NOT contain double bond in it ?
questions.solution:
Tetrahydrofuran is a fully saturated five-membered cyclic ether with the chemical formula $C_4H_8O$. It does not contain any double bonds.

4H-Pyran is a six-membered non-aromatic heterocyclic compound containing one oxygen atom and two double bonds.

Pyrrole is a five-membered aromatic heterocyclic compound containing one nitrogen atom and two double bonds.

Thiophene is a five-membered aromatic heterocyclic compound containing one sulfur atom and two double bonds.

Therefore, tetrahydrofuran is the only compound among the given options that does not contain a double bond.

Answer: Tetrahydrofuran

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds is NOT optically active?
questions.solution:
The optical activity of a compound depends on the presence of a chiral carbon atom, which is bonded to four different groups.

In 3-bromohexane, the C3 carbon is bonded to a hydrogen atom, a bromine atom, an ethyl group, and a propyl group. Since all four groups are different, it is chiral and optically active.

In 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, the C2 carbon is bonded to a bromine atom, an ethyl group, and two identical methyl groups. Since two groups are the same, it does not have a chiral center and is optically inactive.

In 2-bromopentane, the C2 carbon is bonded to a hydrogen atom, a bromine atom, a methyl group, and a propyl group. It is chiral and optically active.

In 2-bromo-3-methylbutane, the C2 carbon is bonded to a hydrogen atom, a bromine atom, a methyl group, and an isopropyl group. It is chiral and optically active.

Thus, 2-bromo-2-methylbutane is not optically active.

Answer: 2 - Bromo - 2 - methylbutane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify substrate 'S' in the following reaction.
$\text{S} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{Na / dry ether}}}$ 3, 4 - diethyl - 3, 4 - dimethyl hexane
questions.solution:
The given reaction is a Wurtz reaction, which involves the coupling of two alkyl halide molecules in the presence of sodium and dry ether to form a symmetrical alkane.

The structure of the product, 3,4-diethyl-3,4-dimethylhexane, is:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)-C(CH}_3\text{)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$

Since the Wurtz reaction produces a symmetrical alkane by the dimerization of alkyl radicals, we can determine the structure of the reactant by cleaving the central carbon-carbon bond of the product.

Cleaving the bond between C3 and C4 yields two identical radicals:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-C}^{\bullet}\text{(CH}_3\text{)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3)$

The corresponding alkyl halide substrate 'S' is formed by attaching a halogen (e.g., chlorine) to the radical carbon:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-C(Cl)(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$

The longest carbon chain has 5 carbon atoms. Numbering the chain from either side gives the same locants, with a chloro group and a methyl group at the 3rd carbon.

Thus, the IUPAC name of the substrate 'S' is 3-chloro-3-methylpentane.

Answer: 3 - chloro - 3 - methylpentane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The major product of the following reaction is
questions.solution:
The given reactant is 3-methylhex-3-ene.

The addition of HI to an alkene is an electrophilic addition reaction that proceeds via the formation of a carbocation intermediate.

First, the electrophile $H^+$ attacks the double bond. This can result in two possible carbocations:
1. Protonation at C-4 yields a tertiary carbocation at C-3.
2. Protonation at C-3 yields a secondary carbocation at C-4.

Since a tertiary carbocation is significantly more stable than a secondary carbocation due to greater hyperconjugation and inductive effects, the reaction proceeds predominantly through the tertiary carbocation at C-3.

Finally, the nucleophile $I^-$ attacks this more stable tertiary carbocation, resulting in the iodine atom attaching to C-3.

The major product formed is 3-iodo-3-methylhexane.

Answer: 3 - iodo - 3 - methylhexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT terminal alkyne ?
questions.solution:
Terminal alkynes have a triple bond at the end of the carbon chain, meaning at least one hydrogen atom is directly attached to a triply bonded carbon atom ($R-C \equiv C-H$).

Ethyne is $H-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

Propyne is $CH_3-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

But-1-yne is $CH_3-CH_2-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

But-2-yne is $CH_3-C \equiv C-CH_3$, where the triple bond is between the second and third carbon atoms. It does not have a hydrogen atom attached to the triply bonded carbon atoms. Thus, it is an internal alkyne, not a terminal alkyne.

Answer: But - 2 - yne

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following aqueous salt solutions has the least pH value ?
questions.solution:
$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is a salt of a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$) and a weak acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$), so its aqueous solution is basic with $\text{pH} \gt 7$.

$\text{CuCl}_2$ is a salt of a weak base ($\text{Cu(OH)}_2$) and a strong acid ($\text{HCl}$), so its aqueous solution undergoes cationic hydrolysis to give an acidic solution with $\text{pH} \lt 7$.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ is a salt of a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$) and a weak acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$), so its aqueous solution is basic with $\text{pH} \gt 7$.

$\text{NaNO}_3$ is a salt of a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$) and a strong acid ($\text{HNO}_3$), so its aqueous solution is neutral with $\text{pH} = 7$.

Therefore, $\text{CuCl}_2$ has the least pH value.

Answer: $\text{CuCl}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic monobasic acid has dissociation constant $1.96 \times 10^{-8}$. What is its percentage dissociation in $0.01$ M solution ?
questions.solution:
For a weak monobasic acid, the dissociation constant is given by $K_a = C\alpha^2$, where $\alpha$ is the degree of dissociation and $C$ is the concentration.

$\alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{K_a}{C}}$

Substituting the given values $K_a = 1.96 \times 10^{-8}$ and $C = 0.01$ M:

$\alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{1.96 \times 10^{-8}}{0.01}}$

$\alpha = \sqrt{1.96 \times 10^{-6}}$

$\alpha = 1.4 \times 10^{-3}$

Percentage dissociation $= \alpha \times 100$

Percentage dissociation $= 1.4 \times 10^{-3} \times 100 = 0.14\,\%$

Answer: $0.14\,\%$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The solubility of salt $\text{AX}_2$ is $6 \times 10^{-12}\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$. What is solubility product of the salt ?
questions.solution:
The dissociation of the salt $\text{AX}_2$ is given by:

$\text{AX}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{A}^{2+} + 2\text{X}^-$

Let the solubility of the salt be $s$.

$[\text{A}^{2+}] = s$

$[\text{X}^-] = 2s$

The solubility product $K_{sp}$ is:

$K_{sp} = [\text{A}^{2+}][\text{X}^-]^2 = (s)(2s)^2 = 4s^3$

Given $s = 6 \times 10^{-12}\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$, substituting this value:

$K_{sp} = 4 \times (6 \times 10^{-12})^3$

$K_{sp} = 4 \times 216 \times 10^{-36}$

$K_{sp} = 864 \times 10^{-36} = 8.64 \times 10^{-34}$

Answer: $8.64 \times 10^{-34}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of chlorine in its weakest oxoacid?
questions.solution:
The oxoacids of chlorine are $HClO$, $HClO_2$, $HClO_3$, and $HClO_4$.

The acidic strength of oxoacids of a halogen increases with an increase in the oxidation number of the halogen atom. As the number of oxygen atoms increases, the electron density is pulled away from the $O-H$ bond, making it easier to release an $H^+$ ion.

The order of acidic strength is $HClO \lt HClO_2 \lt HClO_3 \lt HClO_4$.

Therefore, the weakest oxoacid of chlorine is hypochlorous acid, $HClO$.

Let the oxidation state of chlorine in $HClO$ be $x$.

The typical oxidation state of hydrogen is $+1$ and that of oxygen is $-2$. Since the molecule is neutral, the sum of oxidation states is zero.

$(+1) + x + (-2) = 0$

$x - 1 = 0$

$x = +1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions exhibits the reducing property of ozone ?
questions.solution:
In the reaction $\text{NO}\text{(g)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{NO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, nitrogen is oxidized from $+2$ to $+4$. $\text{O}_3$ acts as an oxidizing agent.

In the reaction $2\text{KI}\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{KOH}\text{(aq)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, iodine is oxidized from $-1$ to $0$. $\text{O}_3$ acts as an oxidizing agent.

In the reaction $\text{PbS}\text{(s)} + 4\text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{PbSO}_4\text{(s)} + 4\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, sulphur is oxidized from $-2$ to $+6$. $\text{O}_3$ acts as an oxidizing agent.

In the reaction $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(l)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, both hydrogen peroxide and ozone undergo mutual reduction. Ozone reduces $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and itself gets reduced to $\text{O}_2$. Thus, this reaction exhibits the reducing property of ozone.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(l)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the use of HDPE ?
questions.solution:
High-density polyethylene (HDPE) is a tough, hard, and rigid polymer. It is widely used in the manufacture of buckets, dustbins, bottles (such as shampoo bottles), and pipes.

Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) is highly branched and flexible, making it suitable for shopping bags, squeeze bottles, toys, and flexible pipes.

Therefore, HDPE is used to prepare shampoo bottles.

Answer: To prepare shampoo bottles

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is a starting material used to obtain viscose rayon ?
questions.solution:
Viscose rayon is a semi-synthetic polymer. It is obtained by the chemical treatment of natural cellulose, which is typically sourced from wood pulp.

The cellulose is first dissolved in an alkaline solution of sodium hydroxide and then treated with carbon disulfide to form cellulose xanthate. This is further dissolved in dilute sodium hydroxide to form a viscous solution called viscose, which is then extruded into an acid bath to regenerate cellulose in the form of fine filaments known as viscose rayon.

Therefore, the starting material used to obtain viscose rayon is cellulose.

Answer: Cellulose

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the use of LDP from following.
questions.solution:
Low Density Polyethylene (LDP) is widely used for the preparation of flexible pipes for agriculture, irrigation, domestic water line connections, and as insulation for electric cables.

High Density Polyethylene (HDP) is used for the manufacture of buckets, dustbins, and rigid pipes.

Teflon (Polytetrafluoroethylene) is used for making non-stick cookware.

Nylon 6 is used for making tyre cords, fabrics, and ropes.

Answer: Preparation of pipes for irrigation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of carbon in oxalic acid ?
questions.solution:
The chemical formula of oxalic acid is $H_2C_2O_4$.

Let the oxidation number of carbon be $x$.

The oxidation number of hydrogen is $+1$ and that of oxygen is $-2$.

The sum of oxidation numbers of all atoms in a neutral molecule is zero.

$2(+1) + 2(x) + 4(-2) = 0$

$2 + 2x - 8 = 0$

$2x - 6 = 0$

$2x = 6$

$x = +3$

The oxidation number of carbon in oxalic acid is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the general formula of halide salts of alkali metals if M is a metal atom ?
questions.solution:
Alkali metals belong to Group 1 of the periodic table and have one valence electron. They lose this electron to form a unipositive ion, $M^{+}$.

Halogens belong to Group 17 and have seven valence electrons. They gain one electron to form a uninegative ion, $X^{-}$.

To form a neutral salt, one $M^{+}$ ion combines with one $X^{-}$ ion.

The general formula of halide salts of alkali metals is $MX$.

Answer: $\text{MX}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A metal forms fcc structure. Calculate the volume of fcc unit cell in $\text{cm}^3$ if void volume is $1.66 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$.
questions.solution:
For an fcc (face-centered cubic) structure, the packing efficiency is $74\%$.

The percentage of void volume in the fcc unit cell is $100\% - 74\% = 26\%$.

Let the total volume of the unit cell be $V$.

Void volume $= $0.26 V$ \\ \\ $0.26 V = 1.66 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$ \\ \\ $V = \dfrac{1.66 \times 10^{-23}}{0.26}\ \text{cm}^3$ \\ \\ $V = 6.3846 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3 \approx 6.385 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$ \\ \\ Answer: $6.385 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of adjacent unit cells shared by each face particle of fcc unit cell ?
questions.solution:
In a face-centered cubic (fcc) unit cell, particles are located at the corners and at the center of each face.

A particle present at the center of a face lies exactly on the boundary between two adjacent unit cells.

Therefore, each face-centered particle is shared equally by exactly $2$ unit cells.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the number of unit cell in $0.5$ g metal if the product of volume and density of unit cell is $6.65 \times 10^{-23}$ g
questions.solution:
Mass of one unit cell is given by the product of its volume and density.

Mass of one unit cell = $6.65 \times 10^{-23}$ g

Total mass of the metal = $0.5$ g

Number of unit cells = $\dfrac{\text{Total mass}}{\text{Mass of one unit cell}}$

Number of unit cells = $\dfrac{0.5}{6.65 \times 10^{-23}}$

Number of unit cells = $7.518 \times 10^{21}$

Answer: $7.518 \times 10^{21}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the molar mass of nonelectrolyte solute when 6 gram of it is dissolved in 1 $\text{dm}^3$ water has osmotic pressure $2.4\ \text{atm}$ at 300 K $(R = 0.0821\ \text{atm dm}^3\ \text{K}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1})$
questions.solution:
The osmotic pressure is given by the formula:

$\pi = C R T = \dfrac{W R T}{M V}$

Rearranging the formula to solve for the molar mass $M$:

$M = \dfrac{W R T}{\pi V}$

Substituting the given values $W = 6\ \text{g}$, $R = 0.0821\ \text{atm dm}^3\ \text{K}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$, $T = 300\ \text{K}$, $\pi = 2.4\ \text{atm}$, and $V = 1\ \text{dm}^3$:

$M = \dfrac{6 \times 0.0821 \times 300}{2.4 \times 1}$

$M = \dfrac{147.78}{2.4}$

$M = 61.575\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Rounding to two decimal places, the molar mass is $61.58\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $61.58\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the mole fraction of solute in solution if vapour pressure of a solution and pure solvent are 27 mm Hg and 30 mm Hg respectively at 298 K.
questions.solution:
According to Raoult's law, the relative lowering of vapour pressure is equal to the mole fraction of the solute.

$\dfrac{P^0 - P_s}{P^0} = x_{\text{solute}}$

Given $P^0 = 30 \text{ mm Hg}$ and $P_s = 27 \text{ mm Hg}$.

$x_{\text{solute}} = \dfrac{30 - 27}{30}$

$x_{\text{solute}} = \dfrac{3}{30} = 0.1$

Answer: $0.1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the number of molecules present in 70 g dinitrogen.
questions.solution:
Molar mass of dinitrogen ($N_2$) is $28 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Number of moles of $N_2$ = $\dfrac{70}{28} = 2.5 \text{ mol}$

Number of molecules = $n \times N_A$

Number of molecules = $2.5 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 1.5055 \times 10^{24}$

Answer: $1.5055 \times 10^{24}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A container contains mixture of He and Ne gases at certain temperature. He is 20 % by mass of mixture. What is the ratio of partial pressure of Helium to Neon ?
questions.solution:
Let the total mass of the mixture be $100$ g.

Mass of He $= 20$ g

Mass of Ne $= 80$ g

Molar mass of He $= 4$ g/mol

Molar mass of Ne $= 20$ g/mol

Number of moles of He, $n_{\text{He}} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5$

Number of moles of Ne, $n_{\text{Ne}} = \dfrac{80}{20} = 4$

According to Dalton's law of partial pressures, the ratio of partial pressures is equal to the ratio of number of moles.

$\dfrac{P_{\text{He}}}{P_{\text{Ne}}} = \dfrac{n_{\text{He}}}{n_{\text{Ne}}} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

Answer: $5:4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following colours has highest energy if wave lengths of violet, blue, yellow and red light are 410 nm, 470 nm, 580 nm and 750 nm respectively ?
questions.solution:
The energy of a photon is given by the Planck-Einstein relation:

$E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

where $h$ is Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light, and $\lambda$ is the wavelength.

From the relation, energy is inversely proportional to the wavelength ($E \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda}$).

The given wavelengths are:
Violet: $410 \text{ nm}$
Blue: $470 \text{ nm}$
Yellow: $580 \text{ nm}$
Red: $750 \text{ nm}$

Since violet light has the shortest wavelength among the given colours, it has the highest energy.

Answer: Violet

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of macromolecular colloid?
questions.solution:
Macromolecular colloids are formed when large molecules (macromolecules) having colloidal dimensions are dispersed in a suitable dispersion medium. Examples include naturally occurring macromolecules such as starch, cellulose, proteins, and enzymes, as well as man-made polymers like polythene, nylon, and polystyrene.

Soaps and detergents are examples of associated colloids (micelles), which are formed by the aggregation of a large number of ions in concentrated solutions.

Sulphur sol, consisting of particles containing a thousand or more $\text{S}_8$ sulphur molecules, is an example of a multimolecular colloid.

Therefore, proteins are an example of a macromolecular colloid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the standard enthalpy change for the following reaction,
$2\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{(g)} + 7\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow 4\text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)}$
Given, $\Delta_f H^\circ(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6) = -85\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta_f H^\circ(\text{CO}_2) = -390\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta_f H^\circ(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = -285\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
questions.solution:
The standard enthalpy of reaction is calculated using the formula:

$\Delta_r H^\circ = \sum \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{reactants})$

For the given reaction:

$\Delta_r H^\circ = [4 \times \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{CO}_2) + 6 \times \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{H}_2\text{O})] - [2 \times \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6) + 7 \times \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{O}_2)]$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta_r H^\circ = [4(-390) + 6(-285)] - [2(-85) + 7(0)]$

$\Delta_r H^\circ = [-1560 - 1710] - [-170]$

$\Delta_r H^\circ = -3270 + 170 = -3100\ \text{kJ}$

Answer: $-3100\ \text{kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct expression of the first law of thermodynamics for adiabatic processes ?
questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, the change in internal energy is given by $\Delta U = Q + W$.

For an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange between the system and the surroundings, which means $Q = 0$.

Substituting $Q = 0$ into the first law equation, we get $\Delta U = W$.

Multiplying both sides by $-1$, this can be written as $-\Delta U = -W$.

Answer: $-\Delta U = -W$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 1 mole of an ideal gas is compressed isothermally and reversibly from initial pressure $x$ kPa to final pressure $2x$ kPa at 300 K. Find the work done $(R = 8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1})$
questions.solution:
For an isothermal reversible process, the work done is given by:

$W = nRT \ln\left(\dfrac{P_2}{P_1}\right)$

Substituting the given values:

$n = 1$ mol

$T = 300$ K

$P_1 = x$ kPa

$P_2 = 2x$ kPa

$R = 8.314$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$

$W = 1 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \ln\left(\dfrac{2x}{x}\right)$

$W = 2494.2 \times \ln(2)$

$W = 2494.2 \times 0.693$

$W \approx 1729$ J

Answer: $1729$ J

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a particle moves such that the displacement (s) is proportional to the square of the velocity (v), then its acceleration (a) is
questions.solution:
Given $s \propto v^2$

$s = k v^2$ where $k$ is a constant.

Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{ds}{dt} = 2kv \dfrac{dv}{dt}$

Since $\dfrac{ds}{dt} = v$ and $\dfrac{dv}{dt} = a$:

$v = 2kv a$

$a = \dfrac{1}{2k}$

Since $k$ is a constant, acceleration $a$ is a constant.

Answer: a constant

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the function $f(x) = ax^2 + bx + \sin x$ satisfies all the conditions of Rolle's theorem on $[0, \pi]$ and the slope of the tangent to the curve $y = f(x)$ at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is zero, then $a - b = $
questions.solution:
Since $f(x)$ satisfies Rolle's theorem on $[0, \pi]$, we have $f(0) = f(\pi)$.

$a(0)^2 + b(0) + \sin 0 = a\pi^2 + b\pi + \sin \pi$

$0 = a\pi^2 + b\pi$

$b = -a\pi$

The slope of the tangent at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is zero, so $f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0$.

$f'(x) = 2ax + b + \cos x$

$f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 2a\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + b + \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0$

$\dfrac{a\pi}{2} + b + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 0$

Substituting $b = -a\pi$:

$\dfrac{a\pi}{2} - a\pi + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 0$

$-\dfrac{a\pi}{2} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 0$

$a = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\pi}$

Using $b = -a\pi$, we get $b = -\sqrt{2}$.

Therefore, $a - b = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\pi} - (-\sqrt{2}) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}(\pi+1)}{\pi}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}(\pi+1)}{\pi}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $g(x) = f(x) + f(1-x)$ and $f''(x) \lt  0, 0 \leq x \leq 1$, then $\ldots$
questions.solution:
Given $g(x) = f(x) + f(1-x)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$g'(x) = f'(x) - f'(1-x)$

It is given that $f''(x) \lt 0$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1$, which implies that $f'(x)$ is a strictly decreasing function on $[0, 1]$.

For $g(x)$ to be increasing, $g'(x) \gt 0$:

$f'(x) - f'(1-x) \gt 0$

$f'(x) \gt f'(1-x)$

Since $f'(x)$ is strictly decreasing, the input values must satisfy the reverse inequality:

$x \lt 1 - x$

$2x \lt 1 \Rightarrow x \lt \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, $g(x)$ is increasing on $\left[0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$.

For $g(x)$ to be decreasing, $g'(x) \lt 0$:

$f'(x) - f'(1-x) \lt 0$

$f'(x) \lt f'(1-x)$

Again, since $f'(x)$ is strictly decreasing, the input values must satisfy:

$x \gt 1 - x$

$2x \gt 1 \Rightarrow x \gt \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, $g(x)$ is decreasing on $\left[\dfrac{1}{2}, 1\right]$.

Answer: $g(x)$ decreases on $\left[\dfrac{1}{2}, 1\right]$ and $g(x)$ increases on $\left[0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area bounded by $y = x^3 + ax$ (where $a  \gt  0$), the $x$-axis and the lines $x = -2$ and $x = 1$ is $\dfrac{37}{4}$ square units, then $\ldots$
questions.solution:
Given the curve $y = x^3 + ax$ with $a \gt 0$, the roots of $y = 0$ are given by $x(x^2 + a) = 0$. Since $a \gt 0$, the only real root is $x = 0$.

For $x \in [-2, 0]$, $y \le 0$, and for $x \in [0, 1]$, $y \ge 0$.

The required area $A$ is given by:

$A = \int_{-2}^{0} -(x^3 + ax) dx + \int_{0}^{1} (x^3 + ax) dx$

$A = -\left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{ax^2}{2} \right]_{-2}^{0} + \left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{ax^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{1}$

$A = -\left( 0 - \left( \dfrac{16}{4} + \dfrac{4a}{2} \right) \right) + \left( \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{a}{2} - 0 \right)$

$A = (4 + 2a) + \left( \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{a}{2} \right)$

$A = \dfrac{17}{4} + \dfrac{5a}{2}$

Given that the area is $\dfrac{37}{4}$ square units:

$\dfrac{17}{4} + \dfrac{5a}{2} = \dfrac{37}{4}$

$\dfrac{5a}{2} = \dfrac{20}{4}$

$\dfrac{5a}{2} = 5 \Rightarrow a = 2$

Answer: $a = 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The number of circles passing through the origin and touching the lines $x + y = 1$ and $x - y = 1$ is $\ldots$
questions.solution:
The given lines are $x + y - 1 = 0$ and $x - y - 1 = 0$.

The center of a circle touching both lines must lie on one of their angle bisectors.

The equations of the angle bisectors are given by:

$\dfrac{x + y - 1}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}} = \pm \dfrac{x - y - 1}{\sqrt{1^2 + (-1)^2}}$

$\dfrac{x + y - 1}{\sqrt{2}} = \pm \dfrac{x - y - 1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Taking the positive sign, we get $2y = 0 \Rightarrow y = 0$.

Taking the negative sign, we get $2x - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 1$.

Case 1: Let the center lie on the bisector $y = 0$. Let the center be $(h, 0)$.

Since the circle passes through the origin $(0, 0)$, its radius is $r = \sqrt{(h-0)^2 + (0-0)^2} = |h|$.

The perpendicular distance from the center $(h, 0)$ to the line $x + y - 1 = 0$ must be equal to the radius $r$.

$\dfrac{|h + 0 - 1|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}} = |h|$

$\dfrac{|h - 1|}{\sqrt{2}} = |h|$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$\dfrac{(h - 1)^2}{2} = h^2$

$h^2 - 2h + 1 = 2h^2$

$h^2 + 2h - 1 = 0$

This is a quadratic equation in $h$ and its discriminant is $\Delta = 2^2 - 4(1)(-1) = 8 \gt 0$. Thus, it has two distinct real roots ($h = -1 \pm \sqrt{2}$). This gives $2$ such circles.

Case 2: Let the center lie on the bisector $x = 1$. Let the center be $(1, k)$.

Since the circle passes through the origin $(0, 0)$, its radius is $r = \sqrt{(1-0)^2 + (k-0)^2} = \sqrt{1 + k^2}$.

The perpendicular distance from the center $(1, k)$ to the line $x + y - 1 = 0$ must be equal to the radius $r$.

$\dfrac{|1 + k - 1|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}} = \sqrt{1 + k^2}$

$\dfrac{|k|}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{1 + k^2}$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$\dfrac{k^2}{2} = 1 + k^2$

$k^2 = 2 + 2k^2$

$k^2 = -2$

This equation has no real solution for $k$. Thus, no circle exists with its center on $x = 1$.

Therefore, the total number of such circles is $2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x) = \dfrac{3^x + 3^{-x} - 2}{\tan x \cdot \log(1+x)}$ for $x \neq 0$, is continuous at $x = 0$, then the value of $f(0)$ is equal to $\ldots$
questions.solution:
Since $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$, $f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$.

$f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{3^x + 3^{-x} - 2}{\tan x \cdot \log(1+x)}$

$f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{3^{2x} + 1 - 2 \cdot 3^x}{3^x \tan x \cdot \log(1+x)}$

$f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{(3^x - 1)^2}{3^x \tan x \cdot \log(1+x)}$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $x^2$:

$f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3^x - 1}{x}\right)^2}{3^x \left(\dfrac{\tan x}{x}\right) \left(\dfrac{\log(1+x)}{x}\right)}$

Using the standard limits $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{a^x - 1}{x} = \log a$, $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\tan x}{x} = 1$, and $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\log(1+x)}{x} = 1$:

$f(0) = \dfrac{(\log 3)^2}{1 \cdot 1 \cdot 1} = (\log 3)^2$

Answer: $(\log 3)^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int_0^2 |4x - 5|\,dx = \ldots$
questions.solution:
The expression inside the absolute value is zero when $4x - 5 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{5}{4}$.

The interval of integration is from $0$ to $2$, so we split the integral at $x = \dfrac{5}{4}$.

$\int_{0}^{2} |4x - 5| dx = \int_{0}^{\dfrac{5}{4}} -(4x - 5) dx + \int_{\dfrac{5}{4}}^{2} (4x - 5) dx$

$= \int_{0}^{\dfrac{5}{4}} (5 - 4x) dx + \int_{\dfrac{5}{4}}^{2} (4x - 5) dx$

Evaluating the first integral:

$\int_{0}^{\dfrac{5}{4}} (5 - 4x) dx = \left[ 5x - 2x^2 \right]_{0}^{\dfrac{5}{4}}$

$= 5\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right) - 2\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right)^2$

$= \dfrac{25}{4} - 2\left(\dfrac{25}{16}\right) = \dfrac{25}{4} - \dfrac{25}{8} = \dfrac{50}{8} - \dfrac{25}{8} = \dfrac{25}{8}$

Evaluating the second integral:

$\int_{\dfrac{5}{4}}^{2} (4x - 5) dx = \left[ 2x^2 - 5x \right]_{\dfrac{5}{4}}^{2}$

$= \left( 2(2)^2 - 5(2) \right) - \left( 2\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right)^2 - 5\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right) \right)$

$= (8 - 10) - \left( 2\left(\dfrac{25}{16}\right) - \dfrac{25}{4} \right)$

$= -2 - \left( \dfrac{25}{8} - \dfrac{25}{4} \right) = -2 - \left( \dfrac{25 - 50}{8} \right)$

$= -2 - \left( -\dfrac{25}{8} \right) = -2 + \dfrac{25}{8} = \dfrac{-16 + 25}{8} = \dfrac{9}{8}$

Adding the two parts together:

$\int_{0}^{2} |4x - 5| dx = \dfrac{25}{8} + \dfrac{9}{8} = \dfrac{34}{8} = \dfrac{17}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int_0^2 x(2 - x)^b\,dx = \dfrac{32}{7}$, where $b \in N$ then $b = $
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int_0^2 x(2 - x)^b \, dx$.

Using the property $\int_0^a f(x) \, dx = \int_0^a f(a - x) \, dx$, we get:

$I = \int_0^2 (2 - x)(2 - (2 - x))^b \, dx$

$I = \int_0^2 (2 - x)x^b \, dx$

$I = \int_0^2 (2x^b - x^{b+1}) \, dx$

Integrating the terms, we get:

$I = \left[ \dfrac{2x^{b+1}}{b+1} - \dfrac{x^{b+2}}{b+2} \right]_0^2$

$I = \dfrac{2 \cdot 2^{b+1}}{b+1} - \dfrac{2^{b+2}}{b+2}$

$I = 2^{b+2} \left( \dfrac{1}{b+1} - \dfrac{1}{b+2} \right)$

$I = \dfrac{2^{b+2}}{(b+1)(b+2)}$

It is given that $I = \dfrac{32}{7}$.

$\dfrac{2^{b+2}}{(b+1)(b+2)} = \dfrac{32}{7}$

Substituting $b = 6$ from the options:

$\dfrac{2^{6+2}}{(6+1)(6+2)} = \dfrac{2^8}{7 \times 8} = \dfrac{256}{56} = \dfrac{32}{7}$

This satisfies the given equation. Therefore, $b = 6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The order and degree of the differential equation $\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}$ are $\ldots$
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

Squaring both sides to remove the fractional powers, we get:

$1 + \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^3$

Multiplying the entire equation by $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$ to express it as a polynomial in derivatives:

$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 1 = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^3$

The highest order derivative present in the equation is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$, which means the order of the differential equation is $2$.

The highest power of this highest order derivative is $3$, which means the degree of the differential equation is $3$.

Answer: Order 2, Degree 3

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A spherical raindrop evaporates at a rate proportional to its surface area. The differential equation involving the rate of change of its radius $r$ with time '$t$' is $\ldots$ (where $k$ is a positive constant)
questions.solution:
Let $V$ be the volume and $S$ be the surface area of the spherical raindrop of radius $r$.

$V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ and $S = 4\pi r^2$

The rate of evaporation is the rate of decrease of volume, which is given to be proportional to the surface area.

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} \propto -S$

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -k S$ (where $k$ is a positive constant of proportionality)

Substituting the expressions for $V$ and $S$:

$\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right) = -k(4\pi r^2)$

$4\pi r^2 \dfrac{dr}{dt} = -k(4\pi r^2)$

Since $r \neq 0$, dividing both sides by $4\pi r^2$ gives:

$\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -k$

$\dfrac{dr}{dt} + k = 0$

Answer: $\dfrac{dr}{dt} + k = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The integrating factor of the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y = x^2 \log x$ is
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y = x^2 \log x$.

Dividing the entire equation by $x$, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{2}{x}y = x \log x$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$, where $P = \dfrac{2}{x}$ and $Q = x \log x$.

The integrating factor (IF) is given by $e^{\int P dx}$.

$\text{IF} = e^{\int \dfrac{2}{x} dx}$

$\text{IF} = e^{2 \log x}$

$\text{IF} = e^{\log x^2}$

$\text{IF} = x^2$

Answer: $x^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The differential equation of the family of all parabolas whose axis is the $y$-axis is $\ldots$
questions.solution:
The equation of the family of all parabolas whose axis is the $y$-axis is given by:

$y = ax^2 + c$

where $a$ and $c$ are arbitrary constants.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2ax$

$\Rightarrow 2a = \dfrac{1}{x} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$, we get:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2a$

Substituting the value of $2a$ from the first derivative into the second derivative, we get:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{1}{x} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\Rightarrow x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

Answer: $x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The rate of disintegration of a radioactive element at any time is proportional to its mass at that time, where $k(k \gt 0)$ is the constant of proportionality. The time during which an original mass of 1.5 gm will disintegrate to a mass of 0.5 gm is $\ldots$
questions.solution:
Let $m$ be the mass of the radioactive element at time $t$.

The rate of disintegration is given by $\dfrac{dm}{dt} = -km$

$\dfrac{dm}{m} = -k dt$

Integrating both sides with appropriate limits:

$\int_{1.5}^{0.5} \dfrac{dm}{m} = -k \int_{0}^{t} dt$

$[\log m]_{1.5}^{0.5} = -kt$

$\log 0.5 - \log 1.5 = -kt$

$\log \left(\dfrac{0.5}{1.5}\right) = -kt$

$\log \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = -kt$

$-\log 3 = -kt$

$t = \dfrac{1}{k} \log 3$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{k}\log 3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f : R \to R$ is an even function then
questions.solution:
Given that $f(x)$ is an even function, we have:

$f(-x) = f(x)$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:

$-f'(-x) = f'(x)$

$f'(-x) = -f'(x)$

This condition satisfies the definition of an odd function. Therefore, $f'(x)$ is an odd function.

Answer: $f'(x)$ is an odd function

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f'(x) = \sin^2 x$ and $y = f\left(\dfrac{2x-1}{x^2+1}\right)$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = 1$ is
questions.solution:
Given $y = f\left(\dfrac{2x-1}{x^2+1}\right)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f'\left(\dfrac{2x-1}{x^2+1}\right) \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{2x-1}{x^2+1}\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f'\left(\dfrac{2x-1}{x^2+1}\right) \cdot \left[ \dfrac{(x^2+1)(2) - (2x-1)(2x)}{(x^2+1)^2} \right]$

Substituting $x = 1$:

$\left. \dfrac{dy}{dx} \right|_{x=1} = f'\left(\dfrac{2(1)-1}{1^2+1}\right) \cdot \left[ \dfrac{(1^2+1)(2) - (2(1)-1)(2(1))}{(1^2+1)^2} \right]$

$\left. \dfrac{dy}{dx} \right|_{x=1} = f'\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \cdot \left[ \dfrac{4 - 2}{4} \right]$

$\left. \dfrac{dy}{dx} \right|_{x=1} = f'\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $f'(x) = \sin^2 x$, we have $f'\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \sin^2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$\left. \dfrac{dy}{dx} \right|_{x=1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}\sin^2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $y = \sqrt[p]{x^3 y}$. If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ when $y = 1$, then the value of $p$ is equal to $\ldots$
questions.solution:
Given $y = \sqrt[p]{x^3 y}$

Raising both sides to the power $p$:

$y^p = x^3 y$

$y^{p-1} = x^3$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$(p-1) y^{p-2} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2$

When $y = 1$, from $y^{p-1} = x^3$, we get $x^3 = 1 \Rightarrow x = 1$.

Substituting $x = 1$, $y = 1$, and $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ into the differentiated equation:

$(p-1) (1)^{p-2} \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = 3(1)^2$

$(p-1) \dfrac{3}{2} = 3$

$p - 1 = 2$

$p = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int f'(x) \cdot e^{x^2}\,dx = (x - 1) \cdot e^{x^2} + k$, where $k$ is constant of integration, then $f(x) = \ldots$
options: $2x^3 - \dfrac{x^2}{2} + x + c$, where $c$ is constant of integration.
$\dfrac{x^3}{2} + 3x^2 + 4x + c$, where $c$ is constant of integration.
$x^3 + 4x^2 + 6x + c$, where $c$ is constant of integration.
$\dfrac{2x^3}{3} - x^2 + x + c$, where $c$ is constant of integration.
questions.solution:
Differentiating both sides of the given equation with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{d}{dx} \left[ \int f'(x) \cdot e^{x^2}\,dx \right] = \dfrac{d}{dx} \left[ (x - 1) \cdot e^{x^2} + k \right]$

$f'(x) \cdot e^{x^2} = 1 \cdot e^{x^2} + (x - 1) \cdot e^{x^2} \cdot (2x)$

$f'(x) \cdot e^{x^2} = e^{x^2} (1 + 2x^2 - 2x)$

Dividing both sides by $e^{x^2}$:

$f'(x) = 2x^2 - 2x + 1$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$ to find $f(x)$:

$f(x) = \int (2x^2 - 2x + 1)\,dx$

$f(x) = \dfrac{2x^3}{3} - x^2 + x + c$

where $c$ is the constant of integration.

Answer: $\dfrac{2x^3}{3} - x^2 + x + c$, where $c$ is constant of integration.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The domain of the function $f(x) = \sqrt{\dfrac{x}{1+x}}$ is $\ldots$
questions.solution:
For $f(x)$ to be defined, the expression under the square root must be non-negative and the denominator must not be zero.

$\dfrac{x}{1+x} \ge 0$ and $1+x \ne 0$

The critical points are $x = 0$ and $x = -1$.

Using the sign scheme for $\dfrac{x}{1+x}$:

For $x \in (-\infty, -1)$, $\dfrac{x}{1+x} \gt 0$

For $x \in (-1, 0)$, $\dfrac{x}{1+x} \lt 0$

For $x \in [0, \infty)$, $\dfrac{x}{1+x} \ge 0$

Since $x = -1$ makes the denominator zero, it is excluded from the domain.

The domain is $(-\infty, -1) \cup [0, \infty)$.

Answer: $(-\infty,-1) \cup [0,\infty)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f(x) = x$, $f_1(x) = f(\log x)$, $f_2(x) = f_1(\log x)$, $f_3(x) = f_2(\log x)$, $\ldots$ and so on. Then $\int \dfrac{1}{f(x)\,f_1(x)\,f_2(x)\,\ldots f_{2026}(x)}\,dx = \ldots$
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = x$

$f_1(x) = f(\log x) = \log x$

$f_2(x) = f_1(\log x) = \log(\log x)$

In general, $f_n(x) = \log(f_{n-1}(x))$.

Differentiating $f_n(x)$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:

$f_1'(x) = \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{1}{f(x)}$

$f_2'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(\log(f_1(x))) = \dfrac{1}{f_1(x)} f_1'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f_1(x) f(x)}$

$f_3'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(\log(f_2(x))) = \dfrac{1}{f_2(x)} f_2'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f_2(x) f_1(x) f(x)}$

By induction, $f_n'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f_{n-1}(x) f_{n-2}(x) \ldots f_1(x) f(x)}$.

For $n = 2027$, we have:

$f_{2027}'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f_{2026}(x) f_{2025}(x) \ldots f_1(x) f(x)}$

The given integral is:

$I = \int \dfrac{1}{f(x) f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_{2026}(x)} \, dx$

$I = \int f_{2027}'(x) \, dx$

$I = f_{2027}(x) + c$

Answer: $f_{2027}(x) + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int e^{x + \tan^{-1}x}\left(\dfrac{x^2 + 2}{\sec^2(\tan^{-1}x)}\right)dx = e^{f(x)} + c$, then $\ldots$
options: $f(x)$ is strictly increasing on $R^+$ and strictly decreasing on $R^-$.
$f(x)$ is strictly decreasing on $R^+$ and strictly increasing on $R^-$.
questions.solution:
The given integral is $I = \int e^{x + \tan^{-1}x}\left(\dfrac{x^2 + 2}{\sec^2(\tan^{-1}x)}\right)dx$.

Using the identity $\sec^2\theta = 1 + \tan^2\theta$, we have $\sec^2(\tan^{-1}x) = 1 + \tan^2(\tan^{-1}x) = 1 + x^2$.

Substituting this into the integral gives:

$I = \int e^{x + \tan^{-1}x}\left(\dfrac{x^2 + 2}{1 + x^2}\right)dx$

$I = \int e^{x + \tan^{-1}x}\left(\dfrac{x^2 + 1 + 1}{1 + x^2}\right)dx$

$I = \int e^{x + \tan^{-1}x}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}\right)dx$

Let $t = x + \tan^{-1}x$. Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$dt = \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}\right)dx$

The integral becomes:

$I = \int e^t dt = e^t + c$

Substituting back $t = x + \tan^{-1}x$, we get:

$I = e^{x + \tan^{-1}x} + c$

Comparing this with the given expression $e^{f(x)} + c$, we find:

$f(x) = x + \tan^{-1}x$

To determine the monotonicity of $f(x)$, we find its derivative:

$f'(x) = 1 + \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}$

Since $x^2 \ge 0$ for all real $x$, $1 + x^2 \ge 1$, which implies $\dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} \gt 0$.

Thus, $f'(x) \gt 1 \gt 0$ for all $x \in R$.

Therefore, $f(x)$ is strictly increasing on $R$.

Answer: $f(x)$ is strictly increasing on $R$.

$\sec^2(\tan^{-1} 3) = 1 + \tan^2(\tan^{-1} 3) = 1 + (3)^2 = 10$
